title: The Basic example credentials published in RFC 7617
summary: The standard's own example Authorization header, whose decoded user-id and password are the RFC's published sample values.
rationale: The standard publishes the value as an example, which suggests a placeholder, but the standard does not say that the value is never a real credential. Treating documented example literals as placeholders is a policy choice, as it is for provider documentation examples, and no maintainer decision is recorded for this one.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 7 (#114), RFC 7617 example): expect it to be unflagged. RFC 7617 publishes this exact header as its example (user-id Aladdin, password open sesame). Only the exact published literal is exempt; any other value is flagged, as for provider example keys. The standard does not say the value is never a real credential. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history.

sources.supports: If the user agent wishes to send the user-id "Aladdin" and password "open sesame", it would use the following header field: Authorization: Basic QWxhZGRpbjpvcGVuIHNlc2FtZQ==

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Maintainer-only (ADR 0020): decided by the sole maintainer, not reviewed, not independent validation; queued for retro-review (#154). Authored from the cited standards read on 2026-10-03, before any scanner was consulted. All values are synthetic and were not tested against any service. Header coalescing, parser and action policy, decoded-token mapping and product masking stay with the downstream repositories.
